clue.text: Take away journalist found in the Channel

indicators.note: something found in a place sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a duct is a channel or conduit
ED is short for editor, the crossword's stock journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter is discovered somewhere in the English Channel, perhaps swept off a ferry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Channel' reads as the sea between England and France, but it is just a conduit.
explanation.definitionFit: To subtract an amount is to take it away, as in deducting tax.

clue.text: Misery for some French couple

parts.note: des is the French for some
a pair is a couple

explanation.surface: A French pair are wretched.
explanation.definitionFit: Despair is utter hopelessness, a form of misery.

clue.text: Father has tea in country house

parts.note: da is a familiar word for father
cha (char) is slang for tea

explanation.surface: Dad takes tea at a house in the country.
explanation.definitionFit: A dacha is a Russian country house or villa.

clue.text: Canon's study includes liturgy and scripture

indicators.note: the first piece includes, takes in, the others

parts.note: to con is to study
a rite is a form of liturgy
RI, religious instruction, is the school scripture lesson

explanation.surface: A cleric's study takes in the order of service and the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canon' suggests a clergyman, but it is a standard or rule.
explanation.definitionFit: A canon is a principle or standard by which things are judged, a yardstick.

clue.text: Accountant pants moving windlass

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant

indicators.note: letters on the move are being shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: An accountant gasps while shifting something heavy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' looks like a verb for breathing hard, but it is only letters for 'moving' to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A capstan is a revolving drum for winding cable on a ship, a kind of windlass.

clue.text: Stop the Spanish officer

parts.note: a colon is a punctuation stop
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Halt the Spanish commander.
explanation.definitionFit: A colonel is a senior army officer.

clue.text: Musician is quiet in supporting part

indicators.note: the quiet letter sits inside the supporting part

parts.note: a pier is a pillar supporting a bridge
P, piano, means quiet in music

explanation.surface: A performer stays quiet in a backing role.
explanation.definitionFit: A piper is a musician who plays pipes.

clue.text: Trial marriage produces international confrontation

parts.note: a test is a trial
a match is a marriage

explanation.surface: Living together before wedding leads to a clash between nations.
explanation.definitionFit: A Test match is an international fixture in cricket or rugby.

clue.text: Madman claims Pluto is barely seen

indicators.note: the madman takes the other piece in, claiming it

parts.note: a nut is a madman
Dis is another name for Pluto, Roman god of the underworld

explanation.surface: A lunatic insists Pluto can scarcely be observed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pluto' suggests the dwarf planet, which is barely visible; it is the god, also called Dis.
explanation.definitionFit: A naturist goes about without clothes, so is seen bare, a playful reading.

clue.text: Closure is imminent, when project leader goes

indicators.note: when something goes it is removed

parts.note: pending means about to happen

indicators.note: a leader comes first, so the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A shutdown is near, now the head of the project has left.
explanation.definitionFit: An ending is a closing or conclusion, a closure.

clue.text: Coastline developed in parts

indicators.note: a coastline that has been developed is reshaped, so its letters are rebuilt in another order

explanation.surface: A shoreline has been built up in some stretches only.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sectional is made in separate sections, that is, in parts.

clue.text: Sat in swimming school round the corner

indicators.note: the outer piece goes round the inner one, enclosing it

parts.note: a pod is a school of whales or dolphins, which swim
SE, south-east, is the corner of a map or compass

explanation.surface: Someone sat down in a swim school just around the bend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimming school' sounds like lessons in a pool, but means a group of whales.
explanation.definitionFit: To sit for an artist or photographer is to pose, so sat matches posed.

clue.text: Informed of fighting in A & E

indicators.note: the fighting is placed in between the two letters given

parts.note: war is fighting

explanation.surface: Someone learned of a brawl in the hospital casualty department.
explanation.walkthrough: A & E (Accident and Emergency) is a British hospital casualty department; here its two letters simply surround WAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Being knowledgeable of something is having been informed of it.

clue.text: Simpleton is disorderly or amusing

indicators.note: disorderly letters are out of their proper sequence, so they get rearranged

explanation.surface: A fool is either unruly or entertaining.
explanation.definitionFit: An ignoramus is an ignorant person, a simpleton or dunce.

clue.text: Soldier hurt still

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, stands for a soldier
a sting is a sharp hurt

explanation.surface: A wounded soldier lies motionless.
explanation.definitionFit: A thing at rest is still, not moving.

clue.text: Huge quantities in Slough? See the publicity!

parts.note: to slough off is to shed
lo is an old word for see
ads are publicity

explanation.surface: Masses of promotion in the town of Slough, look at the posters.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough is a town west of London, but here is the verb to cast off.
explanation.definitionFit: Shedloads is British slang for a great deal, huge amounts.

clue.text: Putting Italian in charge is silliness

indicators.note: putting one thing in another places it inside

parts.note: a levy is a charge or tax

explanation.surface: Appointing an Italian as boss is called foolish.
explanation.definitionFit: Levity is lack of seriousness, frivolity or silliness.

clue.text: Virginia's deceptively lenient sweetheart

parts.note: VA is the abbreviation for the US state of Virginia

indicators.note: letters arranged deceptively are disguised in a new order

explanation.surface: Virginia's beloved only seems easy-going.
explanation.definitionFit: A valentine is a sweetheart chosen on St Valentine's Day.

clue.text: Irish lad gets to church for mystical meeting

parts.note: Sean is an Irish boy's name
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: An Irish boy goes to church for a spiritual gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: A seance is a gathering to contact the spirits of the dead, a mystical meeting.

clue.text: Clearly shows Scene VI is badly written

indicators.note: a badly written piece is jumbled, so the letters are put into another order

explanation.surface: A play's sixth scene is plainly poor.
explanation.definitionFit: To evince a feeling is to display it plainly.

clue.text: Pageant entertained man of honour

parts.note: a gala is a festive show or pageant
to have guests is to entertain them

explanation.surface: A pageant played host to a noble gentleman.
explanation.definitionFit: Galahad was the purest knight of the Round Table, so the name means a chivalrous, honourable man.

clue.text: Garbo hugs man in wedding venue

indicators.note: one piece hugs, encloses, the other

parts.note: Greta Garbo was the film star
N, knight, is a man in chess

explanation.surface: The film star embraces a man at the wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: Gretna Green, just over the Scottish border, was famous for runaway marriages.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish village is a traditional place for eloping couples to marry.

clue.text: Acted without deceased becoming bloated

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: did means acted
late means deceased

explanation.surface: A performance lacking a dead actor swelled up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like a deletion but means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Dilated means expanded or swollen, so bloated.

clue.text: Scratching head, go back to exit

indicators.note: scratching means striking out, so the first letter is dropped

parts.note: to regress is to go back

explanation.surface: Puzzled, someone heads back out the door.
explanation.definitionFit: An egress is a way out or the act of going out.

clue.text: One third of German coal is explosive

indicators.note: a third of a six-letter word is its first two letters

parts.note: lignite is brown coal

explanation.surface: A third of Germany's coal is volatile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One third of' takes GE, the first two of German's six letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Gelignite is a high explosive, a kind of gelatinised dynamite.

clue.text: Girl to stray in woodland

parts.note: G is short for girl
to rove is to wander, stray

explanation.surface: A girl wanders off into the trees.
explanation.definitionFit: A grove is a small wood or group of trees.

clue.text: Plane crashed here

indicators.note: a crashed plane is wrecked, so the word's letters are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A news line: an aircraft went down at this spot.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: the letters of 'Plane' rearranged, and the mountain country where many air crashes happen.
explanation.definitionFit: The Himalayan kingdom has a notorious record of air accidents, so it is a place where a plane crashed.

clue.text: One in a tantrum's a sad subject for a painting

indicators.note: the one is placed in the tantrum

parts.note: a pet is a fit of sulking, a tantrum
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone in a sulk is a gloomy model for an artist.
explanation.definitionFit: A pieta shows the Virgin Mary mourning over the dead Christ, a sorrowful theme in art.

clue.text: Time to muse

parts.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: It is time to reflect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'muse' looks like a verb, ponder, but is the noun: one of the nine Muses.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is the Greek Muse of lyric and love poetry.

clue.text: Sober and satisfied, when outside batting

indicators.note: the first piece sits outside the second, wrapping it

parts.note: content means satisfied
in cricket the side batting is in

explanation.surface: A cricketer is sober and pleased when out in the middle batting.
explanation.definitionFit: Continent means self-restrained or temperate, hence sober.

clue.text: Second year stops logical processes

parts.note: to stem a flow is to stop it

explanation.surface: A sequence of reasoning halts after a second year.
explanation.definitionFit: Systems are orderly methods or procedures, logical processes.

clue.text: Embarrassed about sailor's delay

indicators.note: one piece goes about, around, the other

parts.note: an embarrassed face turns red
a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor is red-faced about his late arrival.
explanation.definitionFit: To retard something is to slow or delay it.
